114 Rafale

• Recently, the defence ministry has initiated discussions on a
  proposal to acquire 114 Dassault Rafale F4 multirole
  fighter jets from France ahead of French President
  Emmanuel Macron’s India visit in February.

• The estimated cost for the jets is Rs. 3.25 lakh crore. This
  could be India’s largest ever defence procurement. This will be
  a government-to-government framework deal.

• The purchase is part of the long delayed Multi-Role Fighter
  Aircraft (MRFA) programme. The proposal shall have to be
  cleared by the Defence Acquisition Council chaired by
  defence minister Rajnath Singh.

114 Rafale


• If executed as planned, the agreement would not only replenish
  the Indian Air Force’s rapidly depleting fighter squadrons but
  also establish India as a global production and maintenance
  hub for the Rafale platform, second only to France itself.

• The fleet composition includes 88 single-seat fighters and
  26 twin-seat trainer variants, all configured for land-based
  operations. All jets are for the use of Air Force only.

• None of the aircraft covered under this proposal are intended
  for naval use, which is already under a separate process to
  induct of Rafale-Marine jets for the Indian Navy.

114 Rafale


• Rs 3.25 lakh crore includes not only the aircraft themselves
  but also a broader package that includes weapons,
  simulators, spares, training, upgrades, industrial
  infrastructure, and long-term maintenance support.

• Once the full order is delivered, the Indian Air Force’s Rafale
  inventory is expected to rise to nearly 150 aircraft.

• India had previously inducted 36 Rafales under a 2016
  agreement, which marked the platform’s first entry into
  Indian service.

114 Rafale


• In parallel, the Indian Navy signed a separate contract in
  April 2025 for 26 Rafale-M jets intended for aircraft
  carrier operations, with deliveries expected to continue into
  the early 2030s.

• Taken together, these acquisitions will result in India
  operating around 176 Rafale fighters across the Air
  Force and Navy.

• This makes India the largest Rafale operator in the
  world and surpassing even the French armed forces in
  terms of total fleet size.

114 Rafale


• A key feature of the MRFA deal is its staggered delivery
  structure, balancing immediate IAF operational needs with
  long-term indigenisation.

• The first 18 Rafale aircraft will be delivered in fly-
  away condition, fully manufactured in France and ready
  for deployment.

• These deliveries are expected to begin around 2030,
  enabling the IAF to replenish squadron strength without
  waiting for domestic production setup.

114 Rafale



• The remaining 96 aircraft will be manufactured in India
  under licensed production.

• A final assembly line will be established at Dassault
  Reliance Aerospace Limited (DRAL) in Nagpur, now a
  subsidiary of Dassault Aviation.

• The Nagpur facility is expected to become a core element of
  India’s combat aircraft manufacturing ecosystem and may
  also support Dassault’s global Rafale supply chain in the long
  term.

114 Rafale


• Indian industry will play a central role in the Rafale F4
  programme, with firms such as Tata Group, Mahindra Group,
  and Dynamatic Technologies Limited, along with over three
  dozen other companies, expected to join the supply chain.

• The indigenisation plan follows a phased model: initial local
  sourcing is projected at around 30%, with a long-term
  target of approximately 60% indigenous content.

114 Rafale


• Dassault Aviation has committed to establishing a comprehensive
  Maintenance, Repair and Overhaul (MRO) ecosystem in India,
  covering full airframe support.

• Safran is expected to set up facilities for the M88 engine powering the
  Rafale. These initiatives aim to reduce lifecycle costs, enhance fleet
  availability, and position India as a long-term sustainment hub for the
  platform.

114 Rafale


• The Rafale C is a single-seat fighter designed for land-based
  air force operations. It is the lightest and most agile variant,
  optimised for air superiority and strike missions.

• The Rafale B is a twin-seat version, also land-based, which
  includes a second cockpit for a Weapon Systems Officer.

   • While initially conceived primarily for training, operational
     experience demonstrated the value of a second crew
     member for complex missions such as deep strikes and
     nuclear deterrence roles.

114 Rafale


• The contract also includes provisions for upgrading Indian
  Rafales to the F5 standard when it becomes available.

• The F5 configuration, expected around 2030, is being
  designed to operate alongside unmanned systems, including
  “loyal wingman” drones, extending the platform’s relevance into
  the next generation of air combat.

• These changes are intended to allow Rafales to operate more
  effectively as part of a connected battlespace, sharing
  information seamlessly with other aircraft, ground stations, and
  command networks.

114 Rafale


• The urgency behind the MRFA deal is driven in large part by the
  Indian Air Force’s declining squadron strength.

• The service is authorised to operate 42 fighter squadrons
  but currently has around 29, a gap that has widened as
  legacy aircraft such as the MiG-21 retire faster than
  replacements can be inducted.

• At the same time, India faces a risky regional security
  environment marked by increased military coordination between
  China and Pakistan. In this context, the Rafale offers a proven
  platform with relatively low integration risk and rapid induction
  timelines.

114 Rafale


• Rafale, introduced in 2001, is a French twin-engine, multirole fighter
  aircraft designed and manufactured by Dassault Aviation, serving both
  the French Air Force and the French Navy (carrier-based operations).

• In 2016, India signed a ₹59,000-crore deal to procure 36 Rafale
  jets after the earlier 126-aircraft MMRCA programme for the IAF failed
  to materialise following nearly seven years of negotiations.

• The MMRCA deal collapsed mainly due to disagreements over
  production arrangements in India. The Rafale acquisition offers greater
  technological advancement, lower lifecycle costs, and specifications
  aligned with India’s operational requirements.

114 Rafale


• Air Supremacy & Multirole Capability: Designed for air
  superiority, interdiction, aerial reconnaissance, ground support, deep
  strike, anti-ship operations, and nuclear deterrence.

• Weapons Package: Equipped with Meteor missile, SCALP cruise
  missile, and MICA missile system.

• Meteor Missile: Next-generation Beyond Visual Range Air-to-Air
  Missile (BVRAAM) with a strike range of ~150 km, capable of
  neutralising enemy aircraft before close engagement.

114 Rafale

• SCALP Cruise Missile: Precision strike capability against land
  targets up to 300 km away.

• MICA Missile System: Versatile air-to-air missile with radar seeker,
  effective from short to long range (up to ~100 km); already deployed
  on IAF Mirages and serves as a primary Rafale weapon.

• Combat Reach: Can engage aerial targets up to 150 km and strike
  ground targets 300 km inside enemy territory, enhancing
  stand-off capability. Accumulated over 30,000 flight hours in service.

114 Rafale


• Strengthens the India–France strategic partnership in the Indian
  Ocean Region, supporting maritime security and countering over-
  flights and WMD-related threats. Substantially augments India’s air
  power amid security challenges from Pakistan and China.

• India becomes the fourth operator after France, Egypt, and Qatar
  to field Rafale as a strategic asset.

• The IAF has also procured the HAMMER (Highly Agile Modular
  Munition Extended Range), a precision-guided weapon developed
  by Safran, for integration with Rafale.

114 Rafale


• Rafale is frequently compared with US fifth-generation fighters
  such as the F-35 Lightning II and F-22 Raptor.

• It is considered more advanced and lethal than China’s Chengdu J-
  20, strengthening India’s preparedness during border tensions.

• The push to acquire the French jets comes amid offers from the
  United States for its F-35 fighters and Russia for the Su-57E aircraft.

114 Rafale



• Defence cooperation forms the core of ties. France is viewed as
  a reliable and technology-sharing partner.

• Major platforms include the Rafale deal and procurement of 26
  Rafale Marine aircraft. Technology transfer enabled India to
  build six Scorpene-class submarine submarines, with three
  more planned.

• Joint Exercises: Exercise Shakti (Army) Exercise Varuna
  (Navy) Exercise Garuda (Air Force).

114 Rafale


• FRIND-X (France-India Defence Startup Excellence) launched
  in line with the vision enshrined in Horizon 2047 and the India-France
  Defence Industrial Roadmap.

• This collaborative platform brings together key stakeholders across
  both defence ecosystems, including defence startups, investors,
  incubators, accelerators, and academia Horizon 2047: roadmap was
  launched on the 25th Anniversary of the India-France
  Strategic Partnership to set the course for the bilateral relationship
  up to 2047.

Two New Telescope
Why in News –

• In the 2026 Union Budget, two new global telescopes has been
  approved in order to expand the observational astronomy along with
  the upgrade of existing global telescope in Ladakh. It is to study the
  sun and origins of the universe.

• The telescopes are named as: (1) National Large Solar
  Telescope (NLST); (2) National Large Optical–Near Infrared
  Telescope (NLOT). The existing global telescope is situated in
  Ladakh which is named as Himalayan Chandra Telescope.

• The Union Budget 2026-27 has earmarked INR 13416.20 crores
  for Department of Science.

Two New Telescope


About the new Telescopes -

• National Large Solar Telescope (NLST):

   • It will be a 2-metre aperture solar telescope built in Merak
     near Pangong Tso, Ladakh.

   • Operates in the visible and near-infrared spectrum to study
     solar magnetism, solar flares, and space weather.

   • Solar activity affects Earth’s satellites, communication
     systems, and space missions.

Two New Telescope

About the new Telescopes -

• NLST:
   • NLST will enhance India’s capability to monitor and forecast
     space weather, protecting national space assets.

   • Expected to be operational in 5–6 years. Will become
     India’s third ground-based solar observatory after
     Kodaikanal Solar Observatory (established 1899) and
     the Udaipur Solar Observatory (established 1975).

   • Will complement data from Aditya-L1, India’s first space-
     based solar mission.

Two New Telescope
About the new Telescopes -

• National Large Optical Near Infrared Telescope (NLOT):

   • It is planned as a 13.7-metre aperture telescope to be
     established at Hanle in Ladakh. Operational in a decade.

   • It will employ a segmented primary mirror made up of 90
     hexagonal segments, integrated to function as a single
     reflective surface.

   • The site’s high elevation, arid conditions, and consistently
     clear skies will reduce atmospheric disturbance, ensuring
     high-resolution observations.

Two New Telescope
About the new Telescopes -

• National Large Optical Near Infrared Telescope (NLOT):

   • The facility will enable cutting-edge studies in:
      • Detection and analysis of exoplanets;
      • Processes of stellar formation and evolution;
      • Investigation of supernova explosions;
      • Research on the early universe and cosmic origins.

   • Once completed, it will be counted among the largest optical–
     infrared telescopes worldwide. India’s involvement in the Thirty
     Meter Telescope (TMT) programme has strengthened its
     technical capability in advanced segmented-mirror systems.

Two New Telescope

About the new Telescopes -

• National Large Optical Near Infrared Telescope (NLOT):

   • India has experience in the ongoing construction of the Thirty Meter
     Telescope (TMT), a major international collaborative project involving
     India, the US, Canada, China, and Japan that aims to significantly
     advance our understanding of the universe.

   • TMT has 494 hexagonal mirror segments across the 30-metre
     primary mirror. India is playing a major role by designing TMT’s
     Segment Support Assembly, a critical component which controls the
     mirror assembly and alignment.

Two New Telescope
About the new Telescopes -

• Existing Himalayan Chandra Telescope (HCT):

   • It is operational for 25 years and is set to be modernised by
     replacing its 2-metre single mirror with a 3.7-metre
     segmented primary mirror.

   • The telescope has made substantial contributions to time-
     domain (transient) astronomy, particularly in tracking brief and
     dynamic phenomena such as supernova events.

   • Post-upgrade, it will conduct observations in the optical and
     near-infrared bands.

Two New Telescope
About the new Telescopes -

• Existing Himalayan Chandra Telescope (HCT):

   • The enhanced HCT will integrate with global research
     infrastructure, including:

      • LIGO-India: An Indo-US collaboration, LIGO-India
        stands for Laser Interferometer Gravitational-Wave
        Observatory, which will comprise an advanced
        gravitational-wave observatory in Maharashtra’s Hingoli
        district.

Two New Telescope

About the new Telescopes -

     • Square Kilometre Array: The Square Kilometre Array is
       an international project to build the world’s largest and
       most sensitive radio telescope across two sites (in
       Australia and South Africa).

  • This advancement will significantly boost India’s capabilities in
    studying gravitational wave counterparts and energetic cosmic
    transients.

Two New Telescope

Significance of new Telescopes -

• Locational Leverage – Situated in Ladakh at a longitudinal position
  underrepresented in existing observatory networks, NLST and NLOT will
  provide sky coverage that complements and extends current global
  capabilities.

• Generation of Frontier Data – The two observatories will deliver high-
  precision, first-hand datasets across solar science, astrophysics, and
  cosmological research, expanding India’s independent scientific
  contributions.

• India’s role in the Thirty Meter Telescope (TMT) project has
  strengthened its expertise in large segmented-mirror systems.

Two New Telescope
Significance of Ladakh -

• Hanle village hosts the Hanle Dark Sky Reserve, India’s first
  officially designated dark sky conservation area.

• The site is characterised by: Negligible light pollution; High elevation
  (~4,500 metres above sea level); Dry and atmospherically stable
  conditions; Predominantly clear skies throughout the year; Optimal
  Observational Nights.

• These factors minimize atmospheric turbulence and enhance
  observational precision, establishing Ladakh as one of the premier
  astronomical locations in Asia.

Nikhil Gupta Case

Why in News –

• Nikhil Gupta, an Indian citizen charged with the 2023 assassination plot
  against Khalistani separatist Gurpatwant Singh Pannun in New
  York, has pleaded guilty in a US court.

• Gupta, aged 54, was arrested in the Czech Republic in June 2023 and
  extradited to the US a year later.

• He pleaded guilty to all three counts in the US Department of Justice’s
  (DoJ) 2024 indictment — murder-for-hire; conspiracy to commit
  murder-for-hire; and conspiracy to commit money laundering. He
  will be sentenced on May 29.

Nikhil Gupta Case

The Case –

• Nikhil Gupta was accused of hiring a hitman - who was, in fact, an
  undercover US law enforcement officer - to kill Pannun in New York,
  making a $15,000 advance payment in May-June 2023.
• Pannun, who holds dual American and Canadian citizenship, heads the
  pro-Khalistan organisation “Sikhs for Justice” which is banned in
  India.

• India has dissociated itself from any plot against Pannun on multiple
  occasions, saying it is against government policy. The Ministry of External
  Affairs has called the allegations “unwarranted and unsubstantiated”.

• India set up a high-level inquiry committee in November 2023 to
  address security concerns raised by the US.

Nikhil Gupta Case


• After US prosecutors accused Gupta of plotting with others to
  kill Pannun, he travelled to the Czech Republic’s capital, Prague,
  from India in June 2023. There, Czech authorities arrested
  him under an extradition treaty between the US and the
  Czech Republic.

• A Czech court rejected his petition to avoid being sent to the US
  in May 2024, clearing the way for the extradition in June 2024.

• Ever since, Gupta has been lodged in a Brooklyn prison and
  maintained his innocence - until now.

Nikhil Gupta Case

Link with Nijjar Assassination -

• The DoJ has drawn multiple links between the Pannun plot and the killing of
  Khalistani separatist Nijjar in Canada on July 18, 2023.

• Quoting FBI Assistant Director Roman Rozhavsky, the DoJ statement
  on Friday said: “The US citizen became a target of transnational repression
  solely for exercising their freedom of speech.”

• “Transnational repression” was the same term used by Canadian
  authorities in the context of their allegations against the Indian government
  over Nijjar’s assasination outside a gurdwara in Surrey, British Columbia. The
  allegations, rejected by India, left bilateral ties in tatters for years.

Nikhil Gupta Case
Who is Pannun -

• Gurpatwant Singh Pannun holds US and Canadian citizenship and
  is a Khalistani separatist.

• Gurpatwant Singh Pannun is an American Sikh political activist and
  lawyer. He is the leading figure of the Khalistan movement in the
  United States and is serving as the general counsel of the
  Sikhs for Justice (SFJ) since 2009.

• Born in the Nathu Chak village in the north-western state of
  Punjab, a young Pannun moved with his parents and siblings to
  Khankot village in Amritsar.

Nikhil Gupta Case



• Pannun has been designated as a terrorist by the Indian
  government since 2020 and was the subject of an assassination
  attempt in 2023.

• In 2020, Pannun was designated as a terrorist by the Government
  of India and his agricultural land was attached under Section
  51A of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, though he
  rejected the charge.

Nikhil Gupta Case


• In October 2022, Interpol rejected India's second request to
  issue a Red Corner Notice on terror charges against Gurpatwant
  Singh Pannun, on the grounds of insufficient information.

• International criminal law and human rights lawyer Richard
  Rogers, who represents Pannun, has accused India of falsifying
  evidence through the Interpol red-notice system.

• A Sikh - a religious minority which makes up about 2% of India's
  population - he says he is an activist who just believes in
  Khalistan.

Nikhil Gupta Case


• India crushed a violent armed Sikh insurgency in the 1980s and
  1990s and the movement has little support in the country now
  although some in the Sikh diaspora continue to advocate for
  Khalistan.

• Pannun and his SFJ are among its most vocal supporters.

• It was only after 2012 that Pannun started getting media
  attention after SFJ began suing prominent Indian politicians and
  celebrities whenever they visited America, accusing them of
  playing a role in the riots.
